note: Alberta Parks recreation area campground on Fallen Timber Creek, 25 km southwest of Sundre off Hwy 22, run by Red Rock Sawmills. Well-treed sites with fire pits and picnic tables, a few by the creek; picnic shelter. The hand pump is for putting out fires only, so bring drinking water. The last 1.5 km of the approach is gravel. OHVs must stay on trailers in the recreation area. --Claude
summary: Confirmed on the AP page (Jul 30, 2026) and Red Rock Sawmill's page: C$40 per unit with firewood, 34 unserviced sites, first-come only, vault toilets, pump water for fires only; season derived 05-01..10-15 -> 05-01..10-13. Stored 'narrow gravel roads - smaller/mid-size rigs' note text had no source and was dropped. Creekside RECOMMENDED (not written): open gravel creek-edge sites by the bridge. Pin across the creek on the road - move suggested.
flags: WATERFRONT (stored not waterfront; recommend creekside with a caveat): AP: 'There are more than 30 well-treed sites, including a few by the riverside.' On Esri imagery and the 2022-04-27 Wayback capture the campground lies in the creek bend south of the TR 310 bridge; its west side is an open gravel/grass flat along Fallen Timber Creek (channel ~20-30 m wide), with an RV parked ~15-20 m from the water across open gravel, and two more units ~20 m from the bank further south among scattered trees. The stored evidence ('loop ~150m+ back... creekside structures are a residence') describes the ranch buildings NW across the creek, not this campground. Site numbers not published. Recommend creekside with a caveat that only a few sites on the west side are by the creek.

PIN (51.6238,-114.7268): on the access road north of the creek, ~130 m N of the campground. Recommend moving to the AP directions point 51.622464,-114.726481 (inside the campground; Red Rock's GPS 51.62256964,-114.726011 is ~35 m from it).

OHV WORDING (not a drop candidate as read): AP: 'it is a good base camp for nearby canoeing, fishing or OHV riding.', 'Please keep OHVs on trailers in the recreation area.' No trail system named or reached from the sites.
